blocks.explanation:
Yahan \(\ln(\sin x)\) aur \(\cos x\) ka product hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
ILATE: L (logarithmic) pehle, is liye \(\ln(\sin x)\) first function, \(\cos x\) second.
Khoobsurat baat yeh hai ke \(\ln(\sin x)\) ka derivative \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) hai, jo \(\sin x\) se zarb ho kar cancel ho jata hai.
Plan: ek dafa parts, phir seedha \(\int \cos x\,dx\). (Doosra raasta: \(u = \sin x\) rakh kar Question 1 wala \(\int \ln u\,du\).)
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \ln(\sin x)\cos x\,dx\), jahan \(\sin x > 0\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: parts: \(f(x) = \ln(\sin x)\), \(g(x) = \cos x\).

Doosre ka integral, pehle ka derivative
\[\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln(\sin x) = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\]
Kyun: chain rule: \(\ln u\) ka derivative \(\frac{u'}{u}\), yahan \(u = \sin x\) aur \(u' = \cos x\).

Parts lagayein
\[= \ln(\sin x)\cdot\sin x - \int \sin x\cdot\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\,dx\]
\[= \sin x\ln(\sin x) - \int \cos x\,dx\]
Kyun: andar \(\sin x\) upar aur neeche cancel ho gaya, sirf \(\cos x\) bacha. Log ab integral se nikal chuka hai.

Integrate karein
\[= \sin x\ln(\sin x) - \sin x + c\]
Kyun: \(\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x\).

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x\ln(\sin x) - \sin x)\]
\[= \cos x\ln(\sin x) + \sin x\cdot\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} - \cos x\]
\[= \cos x\ln(\sin x)\]
Kyun: product rule lagaya; \(+\cos x\) aur \(-\cos x\) cancel ho gaye aur integrand bacha.
